output.brief: The evidence points away from blaming RotaWeave alone, the background checks, or Commonplate. The drop is concentrated at Dock Street and Westgate, which lost their site coordinator on 1 May and use the app. Millbrook has the app but kept its coordinator, and it is stable. Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but has no app, using a paper roster kept by its lead volunteer, and it is nearly flat. So the loss needs both changes together. The basic app tier has no recurring bookings. Coordinators used to book regulars into their usual slots (about 74 a week before May, 3 a week since). Regulars then lost their slots to new sign-ups: 88% of those who lost a slot twice or more are now inactive, against 11% of those who kept theirs. Almost all of those who lapsed had current background checks, and only 2 of 61 callbacks mentioned another group. I'm fairly confident, with the caveat that the booking data comes from a single manager. Next steps: have staff or a trained lead volunteer book regulars into their usual slots before each Thursday release at Dock Street and Westgate, and phone lapsed regulars to offer their slots back. Don't cancel RotaWeave, suspend the checks, or purge the roster. Quarry Lane's October go-live needs the same protection.
output.methodChoice: Problem Analysis plus ACH using site-level IS/IS NOT comparison (X15) and booking reconciliation (X10).
